Great produce doesn’t have to look perfect.

Conventional produce passes through agents, the mandi and a wholesaler before it reaches a kitchen. Every stop adds a markup and a day of shelf life. We removed them.

Pack sizes and pricing matched to what your kitchen actually consumes, rather than one catalogue for everyone.
Procurement sees orders and pricing, finance sees invoices across outlets, chefs see what is cheap today.

Conventional produce moves from the farmer to an agent, then a trader, then the mandi, then a wholesaler, and finally to a business. Each stop takes a margin and a day of freshness, and none of them will take the freeform grades. We replaced that chain with two steps of our own.
Freeform works best where produce gets prepped rather than plated whole — which covers most of a professional kitchen’s volume.
Purées, sauces, dehydrated and ready-to-cook lines, where shape never survives the process.
